info.name: PingFederate ID-JAG - SETUP (admin API) + verify
info.description:
# PingFederate ID-JAG setup collection (for Claude Code or Postman)

Wires up a complete **ID-JAG (Identity Assertion JWT Authorization Grant)** demo on one PingFederate 13.1+ instance
through the PF **admin API**, then verifies it end to end. PF plays both roles: the enterprise IdP that mints the
ID-JAG (token exchange) and the resource authorization server that redeems it (JWT bearer). Everything created is
prefixed with `{{prefix}}` and can be removed with folder **11. Teardown**.

## If you are Claude Code: how to use this file
Read this whole description first, then do the following.

1. **Ask the engineer for these values** (do not guess): PF admin base URL (`pf_admin`, e.g. https://host:9999),
   admin username/password (`admin_user`, `admin_pass`), PF runtime base URL (`pf_runtime`, e.g. https://host:9031).
   Everything else has a working default. Optionally let them pick `prefix` (default `idjag`).
   A brand-new PF install must have its license accepted and the default `Administrator` / `2Federate` password changed
   in the admin console before the API will respond (`license_agreement_not_accepted` means this has not happened yet).
2. **Run the folders in order, 0 to 8, then 10** (skip `0-optional` unless 0c found no signing key). Folder 9 is destructive, see below.
   Preferred runner: `newman run <this-file> --insecure --folder "<folder name>" --env-var pf_admin=... --env-var admin_pass=...`
   (newman may not be installed; if not, execute each request yourself with curl, in order).
   When executing by hand: every admin request needs `-u user:pass`, header `X-XSRF-Header: PingFederate`,
   `Content-Type: application/json`, and `-k` for self-signed certs. Each request's **test script** shows what to check and
   which collection variable it sets (`signing_key_id`, `signing_cert_b64`, `jwks_escaped`, `issuer`, tokens). Apply those
   by hand and substitute `{{var}}` placeholders in later requests.
3. **Idempotence:** creating something that already exists returns 4xx with "already/in use/exists". That is fine, move on,
   but tell the engineer. If an existing object has the same ID but a different definition, ask before changing it.
4. **Folder 9 replaces the PF default authentication policy and turns on IdP authentication policies.** That can break
   the engineer's existing logins. Before running it: run request 9a (backup), tell the engineer exactly what will be
   replaced, and get an explicit yes. If they decline, skip folder 9 and tell them to point their own policy at the
   authentication policy contract `{{prefix}}apc` (the Verify folder still works because it uses the password grant).
5. **Cluster note:** call the admin API on the console (admin) node only.
6. **Report honestly:** list what was created, what already existed, what failed (with the response body), and the result of
   each Verify request. Do not claim success unless folder 10 passes. Do not print passwords/secrets back unless asked.
7. **Hand over:** tell the engineer the client IDs/secrets, the test user, and how to use `10. Verify` / the Postman demo.

## What gets created (all prefixed)
Scopes; Password Credential Validator (+ test user); Authentication Policy Contract; HTML Form adapter; two reference-token
Access Token Managers (user side + resource-AS side); grant and token mappings; OIDC policy; three token processors
(refresh token, access token, ID token); token exchange processor policy; **OAuth Token Exchange SP connection** with
ID-JAG enabled (entity ID = the PF issuer); **IdP connection with OAuth assertion grant** (trusts the PF issuer, signing cert
imported); an auth-code/password/refresh/token-exchange client; a resource-AS client (extension grant); an introspection client.

## Known PF admin API quirks (already handled in the bodies, listed so you can debug)
- Token exchange policy mapping source type is `SUBJECT_TOKEN`; SP connection contract core attribute is `TOKEN_SUBJECT`
  fulfilled from `TOKEN_EXCHANGE_PROCESSOR_POLICY`; IdP OAuth assertion contract core attribute is `TOKEN_SUBJECT`
  (use extended attribute `sub` mapped from `ASSERTION`).
- Refresh Token Processor core attributes: `TOKEN_SUBJECT, client_id, expires_at, scope`.
- PCV-context access token mapping uses context type `PCV`; APC uses `AUTHENTICATION_POLICY_CONTRACT`; the exchange uses `TOKEN_EXCHANGE_PROCESSOR_POLICY`.
- Persistent grant contract only needs `USER_KEY` in the resource-owner mapping.
- PF does not return an ID token on the password grant; it does on the refresh grant (OIDC policy `returnIdTokenOnRefreshGrant`).
- PF may not trust its own self-signed cert, so the ID token processor embeds the JWKS instead of fetching `/pf/JWKS`.
- Authentication policies must be enabled (`enableIdpAuthnSelection`) or the authorize endpoint says "no authentication methods available for OAuth".
- ID-JAG lifetime is about 5 minutes. PF accepted a replayed ID-JAG in testing (no single-use enforcement observed).
- The ID-JAG produced in testing had `typ: oauth-id-jag+jwt`, `iss`, `aud`, `sub`, `resource`; no `client_id` claim was observed.

## Prompt the engineer can paste to Claude Code
> Use the attached Postman collection `PingFederate-IDJAG-Setup.postman_collection.json` to set up ID-JAG on my PingFederate.
> Admin console: https://<host>:9999, admin user `<user>` / `<password>`, runtime https://<host>:9031.
> Read the collection description first, run the folders in order, ask me before the authentication-policy step, and
> finish by running the Verify folder and showing me the results.
